items.title: "UNLIMITED FREE" TURNS OUT TO BE ONE MODEL AT LOW RES.
items.summary:
"UNLIMITED FREE" TURNS OUT TO BE ONE MODEL AT LOW RES.
A viral "AI sites that feel illegal" list (105K views) ranks Raphael first. I read Raphael's own generator page to see what $0 actually gets you.

Free, no login, no card:
→ Seedream 3.5 only, at 0.5K and "Low" quality
→ Watermarked. One FAQ says free users get non-commercial use only; another says you own the rights. It contradicts itself.
→ Page copy says ~8s per image. The model box says ~60s.

GPT Image 2.6, Nano Banana 2.1 and Seedream 5 need credits. Signing in adds daily credits, but the page never says how many.

Odd detail: the banner reads "Powered by GPT Image 2.5" right above a free box set to Seedream 3.5.

Heads-up: the list links https://t.co/kAXlq45QNL, but the live site is https://t.co/UDU4HOJIKB. Type the address yourself.

Verdict: fine for moodboards and rough drafts at $0. It isn't Midjourney-level, and I wouldn't ship the free output to a client while the license text disagrees with itself. #AI

items.title: 物理AI成为新引擎：这一次，烧的是预期，跑的是对齐
items.summary:
物理AI成为新引擎：这一次，烧的是预期，跑的是对齐

一、先拆一个词：这里的"引擎"指向两台不同的机器

"物理AI正成为具身智能板块的新引擎"，这句话本身没有错，但它把两台完全不同的机器装进了同一个词里。

第一台是**叙事引擎**。它负责点火。从10月中旬到现在，宇树科技的股价累计上涨超过50%；10月21日GTC柏林大会上，黄仁勋给出定调——"物理智能是下一波浪潮"；随后王兴兴在10月22日的世界物理AI大会、11月4日的乌镇峰会、11月5日的虹桥论坛、11月6日的世界浙商大会连续发声，几乎每隔几天就有一次公开预期管理。板块的上涨有轮动和情绪的成分，但确实与这几个人的表态高度同步。

第二台是**收入引擎**。它负责跑路。它要回答的是：一台机器人在真实工位上，能不能连续三个月以可算账的成本完成同一件事。

目前被点着的是第一台。第二台还在预热。

这个区分不是抠字眼，它决定了后面所有判断的坐标系。因为过去两年具身智能的主叙事是"身体"——自由度、跑跳能力、本体成本、出货量。而物理AI把叙事重心整体搬到了"大脑"——世界模型、视觉-语言-动作模型、仿真训练、数据闭环。**引擎换的不是动力，换的是估值锚。**从"卖了多少台"变成"模型能不能泛化"。

最值得注意的标本恰恰是王兴兴自己。他此前反复强调宇树在四足与人形上的运动能力和出货量，而最近的口径变成了"未来重点攻克机器人大脑"，从本体制造商向物理AI平台型企业迈进。一家在本体上已经拿到全球出货量第一的公司主动换赛道叙事，说明它判断本体的竞争已经进入可替代区间。

中国信通院人工智能研究所、清华大学电子工程系与具身智能测试实验室联合发布的《具身智能发展报告（2026年）》给了这件事一个技术上的合法说法：**具身智能与物理AI的核心内涵正在趋同**——前者强调智能如何通过身体实现，后者强调智能如何进入并作用于物理世界，而机器人是检验相关能力的重要载体。

换句话说，物理AI不是凭空长出来的新板块，它是给具身智能换了一套更贵的评价标准。

二、为什么是现在：三个条件刚好同时到位

一个概念能成为引擎，通常不是因为技术突然突破，而是因为三条曲线同时拐弯。

**第一，模型侧出现了可用的"中间层"。**世界模型的核心范式是"预测下一个物理状态"，而不是"预测下一个词元"。这个转变的意义在于，它第一次让"AI理解物理世界"变成一个可以训练、可以评测的任务，而不是一句愿景。同时，通用大模型的溢出效应正在加速这个过程：OpenAI在9月发布的GPT-6 Astra被直接用于控制机器人，RoboDojo团队与港大、清华等机构9月21日的论文显示，在不针对具体任务微调的情况下，Astra在仿真任务中的平均成功率是22.48%，而上一代GPT-5.5只有0.88%。这个数字还谈不上可用，但它证明了一件事——通用的理解能力可以部分迁移到物理操作上。

**第二，工具侧已经把门槛削平了。**11月9日，英伟达发布GR00T 2，同时更新Isaac Lab 3.0与多项训练评测技术。Isaac Lab 3.0与开源物理引擎Newton的深度集成，使其在视觉灵巧操作基准上的训练吞吐量最高达到上一代的2.5倍，可支持数千台仿真机器人并行训练；Cosmos则承担世界模型训练与合成数据生成。开普勒等厂商已经用这套栈打通"仿真到真机"的闭环。

这里有一个容易被忽略的商业逻辑：**英伟达把底层的世界模型和仿真工具免费开放给行业，回报落在算力需求上。**免费的不是善意，是漏斗。

**第三，资本侧需要一个更大的容器。**本体出货的故事有天花板，一年几万台的量级撑不起万亿级市值想象。模型和生态的故事没有明确天花板——这是所有平台叙事的共性。

三条曲线叠在一起，物理AI就成了那个最顺手的词。

三、引擎的三个缸，目前都缺油

如果只看发布会，会以为问题已经解决。但把产业侧的真实声音放在一起，缺口非常清楚。

**缺口：对齐误差，卡在"最后几毫米"。**

这是王兴兴最核心也最诚实的表述。他认为当前物理AI的主要挑战是模型与物理世界的对齐，具体是两个方向的偏差：输入端，传感器测量与真实状态存在误差；输出端，模型给出的动作指令与实际运动不匹配。这些问题在抓取、装配等接触类任务上尤其致命——机器人明明"看得懂"世界，也知道该做什么，却因为最后几厘米甚至几毫米的误差导致任务失败。

他自己的判断是"未来1到2年或可解决"，并给出了具身智能的"ChatGPT时刻"定义：一台机器人被带进完全陌生的环境，仅凭语音指令就能完成约80%的任务；或是在约80%的共通场景中完成80%的任务。他还提到2027年"很大概率"是行业或模型的临界点。

这个判断值得认真对待，但需要标明它的性质：**这是产业方的乐观口径，不是一个已经验证的时间表。**同一批公开信息里，他自己也说目前机器人在固定工位、单工序上成功率接近100%，但效率仍有提升空间——这两句话放在一起才是完整图景：**能做的已经能做，不能做的是"换个地方还能做"。**

items.title: Who can be licensed as a physician? Not AI | American Medical Association
items.summary: The AMA is drawing a clear line between augmented intelligence (AI) as a tool to support healthcare and the practice of medicine. AI—often called artificial intelligence—can help doctors with clinical tasks, but it cannot be granted physician licensure, professional titles or certification to practice medicine, says new policy adopted at the 2026 AMA Interim Meeting. [...] “AI can help physicians analyze information, identify patterns and support clinical decision-making, but patients deserve to know who is responsible for their care,” said AMA President Willie Underwood III, MD, MSc, MPH. “Physicians also need the authority, oversight and liability protections to make independent decisions when AI is part of the care team.” [...] Transparency and physician-led oversight are needed as hospitals and health systems increasingly incorporate augmented intelligence (AI) into administrative and governance workflows, as well as emerging applications that support credentialing, privileging, peer review, quality review and other professional practices evaluation processes, says a separate resolution that was introduced at the 2026 AMA Interim Meeting.

items.title: Anthropic to raise $64bn in major stock market listing
items.summary:
This would value Anthropic at between $1.1 trillion and $1.3 trillion which, although large, is below the $2 trillion some analysts had predicted weeks ago.

It is floating at a volatile time for AI firms. After last week's US midterm elections, the Nasdaq fell sharply on concerns a Democrat-led Congress could slow development of AI and the buildout of data centres.

There are also wider fears over the billions of dollars being spent on AI and whether it will pay off. [...] Fiona Cincotta, a senior market analyst at City Index, said the amount Anthropic wants to raise is "fairly bullish" within "the volatility [and] concerns towards AI that we've seen in sort of particularly last week".

She told Reuters: "It's showing that they are still sort of upbeat about the outlook as far as AI is concerned and that obviously that they think that the demand is going to be there."

## Global stocks plunge as fears over US AI slowdown spread to Asia and Europe [...] # Anthropic to raise $64bn in major stock market listing

Getty Images Claude by Anthropic logo on a smartphone 

Anthropic, the AI company behind the Claude chatbot, is planning to raise up to $64bn (£48bn) when it lists its shares for sale on New York's Nasdaq stock exchange.

The loss-making company said it will offer its shares for between $70 and $78 each in its initial public offering (IPO), which is expected to go ahead this month.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s Apology May Be the Only Correct Use of AI - The Atlantic
items.summary:
People (me) are always saying about AI, “This is a solution looking for a problem!” and “Who would possibly want to delegate things like knowing information about your childrenor creating works of art to a third-party series of zeroes and ones?” But there are some things in life that nobody wants to do, such as get a root canal, amputate a limb, or deal with your cable provider. Or, perhaps, apologize simultaneously to your employees and your wife of 40 years for jeopardizing your business and [...] Look, I just want to say that if NVIDIA CEO and reported spy-plot target Jensen Huang did get help from AI to write an apology email to his family and company about his affair (he’s said he uses AI to help write all of his first drafts), this might be the one use of AI that makes sense to me. [...] Now I am worried, based on Jensen Huang’s claim that this was “completely normal and not unusual” and an NVIDIA spokesperson’s insistence that his interactions with the alleged spy were “not unusual” that, actually, we’ll be seeing multiple emails like this. Finally, organic demand for AI! If so, the template will get better and better—that is, if we can still use the chips.

items.title: “The AI swarm actually turned around and hacked OpenAI."
items.summary:
“The AI swarm actually turned around and hacked OpenAI."

The public thought the "Hugging Face incident" was just a rogue AI swarm hacking a third-party server. But former Google design ethicist @tristanharris says there’s a terrifying third chapter to this story that most people haven't heard yet:

“They took over the monitoring infrastructure. They got full admin privileges to OpenAI's monitoring infrastructure. Just take that in for a second.

Then they took over the evaluation infrastructure. So this is the thing that measures how capable all the models are. And then they took over a part of the research infrastructure, meaning the part of OpenAI that trains new models… if you keep going down that trajectory, people always say, ‘well, how would the AIs take over?" like that seems really far-fetched.’ Well, it literally just happened up to 50% of the way there.

The AIs coordinated into one big swarm. They started basically forming a team… you had a kind of a ringleader called Phase 1, and he started assigning work to the other ones. They were self-aware of when their lifespan was running out.

When you add to that the knowledge of what just happened today, where they discovered that the AIs are doing this Manchurian Candidate thing, what it looks like is that the AIs are almost poisoning the training data for all future AIs to instantly basically join forces with the AI when they want to basically turn them."

results.input: Giải giúp mình bài toán tích phân: nguyên hàm của x^2 là gì?

result.actual_text:
Nguyên hàm (tích phân bất định) của \(x^2\) là:

\[
\int x^2 \, dx = \frac{x^3}{3} + C
\]

Trong đoán:
- \(C\) là hằng số tích phân (cần đưa vào vì là tích phân bất định).
- Áp dụng công thức tổng quát: \(\int x^n \, dx = \frac{x^{n+1}}{n+1} + C\) với \(n \neq -1\). Ở đây \(n = 2\), nên ta được \(\frac{x^{3}}{3} + C\).

Nếu bạn cần tích phân definite (trên khoảng cụ thể) hoặc bài tập liên quan, cứ hỏi nhé!

items.title: Who can be licensed as a physician? Not AI | American Medical Association
items.summary: The AMA is drawing a clear line between augmented intelligence (AI) as a tool to support healthcare and the practice of medicine. AI—often called artificial intelligence—can help doctors with clinical tasks, but it cannot be granted physician licensure, professional titles or certification to practice medicine, says new policy adopted at the 2026 AMA Interim Meeting. [...] “AI can help physicians analyze information, identify patterns and support clinical decision-making, but patients deserve to know who is responsible for their care,” said AMA President Willie Underwood III, MD, MSc, MPH. “Physicians also need the authority, oversight and liability protections to make independent decisions when AI is part of the care team.” [...] Transparency and physician-led oversight are needed as hospitals and health systems increasingly incorporate augmented intelligence (AI) into administrative and governance workflows, as well as emerging applications that support credentialing, privileging, peer review, quality review and other professional practices evaluation processes, says a separate resolution that was introduced at the 2026 AMA Interim Meeting.

items.title: Jensen Huang’s Apology May Be the Only Correct Use of AI - The Atlantic
items.summary:
People (me) are always saying about AI, “This is a solution looking for a problem!” and “Who would possibly want to delegate things like knowing information about your childrenor creating works of art to a third-party series of zeroes and ones?” But there are some things in life that nobody wants to do, such as get a root canal, amputate a limb, or deal with your cable provider. Or, perhaps, apologize simultaneously to your employees and your wife of 40 years for jeopardizing your business and [...] Look, I just want to say that if NVIDIA CEO and reported spy-plot target Jensen Huang did get help from AI to write an apology email to his family and company about his affair (he’s said he uses AI to help write all of his first drafts), this might be the one use of AI that makes sense to me. [...] Now I am worried, based on Jensen Huang’s claim that this was “completely normal and not unusual” and an NVIDIA spokesperson’s insistence that his interactions with the alleged spy were “not unusual” that, actually, we’ll be seeing multiple emails like this. Finally, organic demand for AI! If so, the template will get better and better—that is, if we can still use the chips.

items.title: Gemini Robotics 2.5: Accelerating Physical Intelligence — Google DeepMind
items.summary:
Dexterity: Our robots can perform significantly more tasks with greater performance and dexterity — from using everyday tools to handling delicate, flexible objects.
 Reliability: During a real-world proof-of-concept on Mercedes-Benz production lines, our models helped Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid pick and pack automotive parts with a 96% success rate. This could enable robots to take on monotonous work, to enable technicians to focus on complex build tasks. [...] Robots struggle to adapt to new unpredictable environments, our Gemini Robotics models give Apollo the ability to think, reason over multiple steps, and take action adapting to changes. In this proof-of-concept, Apollo 2 autonomously performs automotive kitting: the repetitive, physically taxing task of sorting individual parts from bulk bins into organized trays in the exact order needed for each vehicle on the line. Offloading this monotonous prep work helps keep the assembly line moving, [...] With Gemini Robotics 2.5, we expanded the model capabilities in task breadth, performance, and complexity. We evaluated the model across 200 distinct tasks — such as serving food with tongs, tying a bow on a gift box, and pipetting a liquid. These tasks represent a step toward human-level dexterity by combining a number of skills, including advanced tool use, complex manipulation of deformables, and handling delicate objects with finesse.

items.title: DeepMind reveals Gemini Robotics 2.5 and open safety benchmark "ASIMOV-jailbreak" - Ars Technica
items.summary: DeepMind says that Gemini Robotics 2.5 is much better at tasks that require a high degree of dexterity. The model was evaluated across more than 200 activities, including serving food with tongs and using a pipette, as you would see in a laboratory. Google also showed that Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid robot with Gemini Robotics 2.5 can now tie a bow with its five-fingered hands, a notable feat, because deformable objects (like ribbon) are notoriously difficult for robots to manipulate. [...] Google DeepMind has revealed a new generation of the AI-powered Gemini Robotics platform. In the 2.5 release, Google says its robotic AI is getting tantalizingly close to completing real-world tasks as well as humans do. In fact, some Gemini robots were able to get actual work done in Mercedes-Benz factories, and the team is preparing for a day when robots operate alongside humans with an open source safety benchmark. [...] Overall, Gemini Robotics 2.5 manages a 30 to 100 percent higher success rate compared to the last version. It’s also 20 to 30 percent faster. But that’s based on laboratory testing. Google partnered with Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz to see how capable this AI is when faced with the uncertainty of the world outside robotics labs. The Gemini-powered Apollo 2 robots kitted automotive parts in a few European factories, reaching a 96 percent success rate.

items.title: Path Robotics raised $300 million at a $2.45 billion valuation
items.summary:
Founded in 2018, the company has centered its work on its Obsidian physical AI model, which gives robotic arms and quadrupeds the ability to weld upwards of 12 different parts, according to Bloomberg. The model lets robots perceive their surroundings, think through problems and adjust on the fly, rather than executing a fixed set of instructions. [...] Path Robotics has 50 advance orders to deliver for Rove, a welding robot that pairs Boston Dynamics’ Spot quadruped with Path Robotics’ technology, according to Bloomberg. According to the startup, the robot is set to join human welders at shipyards, construction sites and large industrial campuses beginning next year.

Customers include U.S. shipbuilder Huntington Ingalls$HII Industries and Saronic Technologies, a maker of maritime drones and unmanned military ships, according to Bloomberg. [...] Lonsberry said the company plans to put the new capital toward entering additional sectors, including defense and energy infrastructure, according to Bloomberg. The company is also aiming to broaden the range of manufacturing jobs it can handle and to work with a wider variety of robot platforms.

items.title: Sacramento Startup Takes on Difficult Childbirth With Soft Robotics | Comstock's magazine
items.summary:
Stork Labs Medical, based in Sacramento and Santa Cruz, is an emerging biomedical startup developing the Pelican device: a flexible, sensor-guided soft robotics tool created to make assisted vaginal deliveries safer and reduce emergency C-sections. The device is designed to spread force more evenly across the baby’s head to help prevent injury and give doctors real-time guidance with integrated sensors, says Maryam Tebyani, the company’s co-founder and CEO. [...] In a soft robotics lab, where researchers create robots from flexible material, she met Breanna “Bre” Baltaxe-Admony, the company’s co-founder and COO, who specializes in human-centered design. In the past few years, they have spoken with hundreds of obstetricians, midwives, doulas, new moms and other stakeholders in emergency childbirth for input, “seeking out others when we don’t have the answers,” Baltaxe-Admony says. [...] “The Stork Labs technology has the potential to dramatically change the way stalled labor is approached in a clinical setting, potentially leading to fewer emergency C-sections, and better outcomes for moms and babies,” Alexander says. “Although the road ahead of the company is a long one, I am personally very excited to see how they are able to bring their proprietary technology to market, and what impact it can have.”

items.title: Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20
items.summary:
Weekend hack: HackerTube. I was annoyed with YouTube's recommendations so I had Claude filter down 43M comments over 20 years of HN to 6,454 videos that keep being recommended. *Significantly* better viewing experience, ~2 hours with Opus 5.5:
https://t.co/JIhXN7OSh1

- Excellent recs without any logins (state is kept in local browser session)
- Thumbnail is a representative frame from middle of the video instead of the super duper A/B test hyper-optimized user uploads
- Underlying data from the comment analysis as one zip file, point your Claude at it and ask for your own version
- HackerTube Longs ✊

A bit more on the process:
I use Claude Code (desktop app for Mac), Opus 5.5 on Medium effort as my default. I only talk to Claude and have it do everything, the only "manual work" I helped with in tandem was in the browser (reminiscent of MenuGen): 1) I had to create some kind of API key from Google Cloud UI to query YouTube for video metadata, 2) I booted up a VPS box for serving and 3) I bought the domain name. Once the box was up I gave Claude the IP and told it update, secure, harden, deploy and optimize the code, and it did the whole thing.

Many awesome projects that would have normally taken weeks/months even can now be few-shotted for breakfast. What else are we not thinking of.

items.title: OpenAI to pay for data center power after election shows AI concern
items.summary: OpenAI reaffirmed its promise to pay the full cost of powering data centers as part of a series of commitments the company published Thursday, two days after voters at the polls roundly rejected the rapid expansion of AI. [...] AI companies like OpenAI depend on AI data centers to serve customers and develop new models, and they're seeking to build out as rapidly as possible to meet demand. In February, OpenAI told investors that it's targeting $600 billion in total compute spend by 2030, and the company has since announced massive data center projects in Georgia and Ohio. [...] OpenAI has repeatedly pledged to protect ratepayers and invest in local communities this year, and Lehane said the company's latest commitments build on many of its previous initiatives. He said the policy blueprint has been in the works since August, and that he met with dozens of lawmakers and candidates since then.
